q-43109.name: Question 1
q-43109.problem:

$$

$$

q-43109.worked_solution:
We are given the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}5x+(-8)y+3z=2 \\ 0x+6y+(-3)z=-7 \\ 1x+(-5)y+4z=-10.\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
D=|\begin{aligned}5 & -8 & 3 \\ 0 & 6 & -3 \\ 1 & -5 & 4\end{aligned}|.
$$

Now, to construct ${D}_{y}$, we replace the second column of the coefficient matrix by the right-hand side column of the given system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y}=|\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -7 & -3 \\ 1 & -10 & 4\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}2-k & =-5 \\ k & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $⟨x,y,z⟩$ be the unique solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}5x-3y-z=1 \\ x+4y+kz=-1 \\ 2x+3y+4z=9.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that  $z=1$ and that the determinant of the coefficient matrix is equal to $97-21k,$ find the value of $k.$

First, let's write the determinant of the coefficient matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}D=|\begin{aligned}5 & -3 & -1 \\ 1 & 4 & k \\ 2 & 3 & 4\end{aligned}|=97-21k\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $z$ is given by $z=\frac{{D}_{z}}{D},$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{z}=|\begin{aligned}5 & -3 & 1 \\ 1 & 4 & -1 \\ 2 & 3 & 9\end{aligned}| & =5\cdot |\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ 3 & 9\end{aligned}|-(-3)\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 9\end{aligned}|+1\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =5(36+3)+3(9+2)+(3-8) \\  & =195+33-5 \\  & =223.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
z=\frac{{D}_{z}}{D}=\frac{223}{97-21k}.
$$

From the problem statement, we know that $z=1.$ So, we can solve for $k$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{223}{97-21k} & =1 \\ 223 & =97-21k \\ 21k & =-126 \\ k & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $⟨x,y,z⟩$ be the unique solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}6x+5y-3z=2 \\ 4x-5y+kz=1 \\ -2x+10y-5z=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

First, let's write the determinant of the coefficient matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}D=|\begin{aligned}6 & 5 & -2 \\ 4 & -5 & k \\ -2 & 10 & -5\end{aligned}|=160-70k\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $x$ is given by $x=\frac{{D}_{x}}{D},$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{x}=|\begin{aligned}2 & 5 & -3 \\ 1 & -5 & k \\ -2 & 10 & -5\end{aligned}| & =2\cdot |\begin{aligned}-5 & k \\ 10 & -5\end{aligned}|-5\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & k \\ -2 & -5\end{aligned}|+(-3)\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -5 \\ -2 & 10\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(25-10k)-5(-5+2k)-3(10-10) \\  & =50-20k+25-10k+0 \\  & =75-30k.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
x=\frac{{D}_{x}}{D}=\frac{75-30k}{160-70k}.
$$

From the problem statement, we know that $x=\frac{1}{2}.$ So, we can solve for $k$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{75-30k}{160-70k} & =\frac{1}{2} \\ 2(75-30k) & =160-70k \\ 150-60k & =160-70k \\ 10k & =10 \\ k & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
